theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Energy (+1.20%) and Utilities (+1.04%) led the market today, while Real Estate (-0.67%) and Consumer Discretionary (-0.63%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -0.37% versus +0.30% for defensives and +0.24% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -0.32%, Dow -0.34%, Nasdaq -0.60% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up +0.32%, outperforming large caps. The VIX fell 1.16% to 15.28, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold slipped 1.10% to $4,427.80, crude oil was little changed at $83.23, and bitcoin slipped 0.49% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
